RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are men, making it exceedingly unlikely that sex bias influenced the decision against you. Raising the panel's gender composition as a grievance will appear unfounded and could damage your professional reputation within the civil service.

While an all-male panel may conflict with public sector diversity guidelines or best recruitment practices, it does not substantiate discrimination between two male applicants. The appointment likely turned on specific role requirements—such as the other candidate's international project leadership—or interview performance. 

Instead of questioning the panel's composition, send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback to understand how the panel evaluated your specific competencies against the successful candidate.
